title: Symmetry Breaking in Standard Event Side Effects
pattern: A controller or coordinator class executes similar state-altering operations, but some paths fail to perform the standard cross-cutting side effects (such as event publication, audit logging, or cache invalidation) implemented by the others.
why_bad: It breaks the expected structural symmetry of use cases. Downstream subsystems that rely on the missing side-effect (e.g., updating shipping details on labels when the address is updated) are silently left in an inconsistent state.
detection: Analyze methods of a single service or manager that write to a database. Flag any method that does not invoke the same event-publishing or auditing channels used by other writing methods in that same class.
counterexample: Operations that are explicitly local and documented as having zero external side-effects (e.g., intermediate drafts). Marked `Context-dependent`.
fix: Restore structural symmetry by dispatching the corresponding `OrderAddressUpdated` event in the update method.
